title: AI Readiness Framework
tagline: Know where you are before you decide where to go
summary: Most organizations rush to implement AI before they're ready, and wonder why it doesn't stick. This framework helps leaders assess readiness across four dimensions — not to find reasons to delay, but to identify the highest-leverage changes that unlock adoption.

pillars.name: Infrastructure
pillars.description: Do you have the data, compute, and security foundations to run AI systems responsibly? This isn't about having everything perfect — it's about knowing what you have and what the gaps are.

pillars.name: People
pillars.description: Do your teams have the AI literacy to use tools effectively and the psychological safety to experiment? The biggest barrier to AI adoption is usually human, not technical.

pillars.name: Process
pillars.description: Do your workflows create natural integration points for AI, or do they require people to break their habits to use it? AI that fights your process dies in a drawer.

pillars.name: Culture
pillars.description: Is leadership modeling curiosity about AI, or sending signals that errors are failures? Cultures that treat AI experiments as learning opportunities adopt faster than those that demand certainty.

keyQuestions: Where in your workflow does AI create the most immediate leverage?
What's the biggest fear your team has about AI — and is it grounded in reality?
What would need to be true for your team to use AI on Monday morning?
Who are your early adopters, and how can they help the rest of the team?
exampleInPractice: In enterprise workshops, I use a quick 20-question readiness survey across these four pillars. Teams score themselves and immediately see patterns — most organizations are strong in infrastructure but weak in culture, or vice versa. That gap becomes the roadmap. [NEEDS REVIEW BY MARLON]
